key_facts: Airbnb has updated its rules to limit what hosts may ask guests to do, including cleaning tasks. Hosts can set seven standard house rules and add other "reasonable" requests.

Hosts are generally not allowed to ask guests to complete tasks that "require significant effort or time, or would typically be performed by a cleaner, including stripping the bed, taking trash offsite, or washing and putting away dishes". Contracts are allowed only in limited circumstances (e.g., when required by law or homeowners association rules). Hosts cannot impose fines; requests not following Airbnb policy are flagged and owners can appeal.

actors: University of Queensland Cyber Research Centre
key_facts: Serious vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language, undetected for more than a decade, were found with the help of AI tools by researchers at Wiz and Calif, prompting a global cyber-security alert.

The flaw could allow attackers to take control of affected web servers without authentication and steal sensitive data; Wiz described it as the "most severe" ever detected by AI, and OpenAI called it "one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory".
PHP powers a large number of platforms, including online shops, Wikipedia and WordPress; Gorilla Cyber Security's chief executive estimated the flaw could affect "millions and millions" of websites.

PHP developers released patches on Wednesday; the US NSA advised organisations unable to patch immediately to take their systems offline, and the UK NCSC issued similar guidance. Wikimedia, the Finnish government, Edinburgh council and the BBC took some sites offline as a precaution.
importance_reason: Widespread cyber-security incident affecting a foundational web technology with government-level response, but it is not a direct market or macroeconomic event.
